Continue the public server directory work for Nxeon and extend it beyond Steam. Notes to /root/agent-notes/directory-v2.md as you go; final report at the end.

HARD RULES: read /root/agent-briefs/growth-batch-2026-10-02.md first, all its rules apply (no prod DB writes, no node/VM changes, no secrets in logs, explicit-path commits, never `git add -A`, build in a git worktree on /tank off main e.g. `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/nxeon-wt-dir2 -b feature/directory-multisource main`, cp -a node_modules, dummy DATABASE_URL for prisma generate, heavy lock, no builds in /opt/nxeon). Schema changes must be additive only. Do not merge to main; the owner session integrates. Do not set any production flag or run any ingest against prod. Third-party sources: only read public data you are allowed to read; honour robots.txt, each source's terms of service and rate limits, send an honest User-Agent, cache aggressively, never hammer. If a source forbids scraping or needs a paid or approved key, do not scrape it: record it as BLOCKED with the reason and an alternative.

STATE: Phase 1 is on main and deployed 2026-10-04 (lib/directory-*.ts, lib/directory-ingest/, lib/directory-steam.ts, lib/directory-blocklist*.ts, ExternalServer + DirectorySource tables, A2S prober, block-other-hosting-providers matcher, worker scheduling). Plan: /root/research/directory-v2-plan.md. Prod facts (read-only): ExternalServer has 0 rows; DirectorySource 'steam' has lastOkAt null and no error, so the Steam import has NEVER run; settings directory_ingest_enabled=true and directory_external_show=true. The owner looked at the customer portal public-server page and says it looks the same as before: confirm why (page code, query filters, flags, empty table) and make the page really show external servers when present.

TASKS:
1. Diagnose, read-only, why the Steam ingest never ran (worker schedule, circuit breaker, runRequested, missing STEAM_WEB_API_KEY or other env, a feature flag, an error swallowed). Report the exact cause and the minimal fix, and say what the owner must do (e.g. set a key) versus what code must change.
2. Inventory every game family in lib/games.ts GAME_FAMILIES (about 55). For each, find the best COMPLIANT public source of live public servers: Steam Web API / master server (IGameServersService/GetServerList, appid filters, include the games that use Steam's master), BattleMetrics public API (check its terms, rate limits, key requirements, attribution), the FiveM public servers API, Minecraft Java and Bedrock (check what lists permit programmatic access; direct SLP pings of addresses we already know are fine), Terraria, Palworld, Valheim, Rust, ARK, Project Zomboid, 7 Days, DayZ, CS2, TF2, L4D2, GMod, Factorio (official matchmaking API), Satisfactory, Don't Starve Together, V Rising, Enshrouded, etc. Produce a table in docs and /root/research/directory-sources.md: family, source, access method, ToS/robots verdict, rate limit, key needed, attribution text, liveness method (A2S, SLP, RakNet, HTTP), and BUILD / BLOCKED.
3. Implement adapters for every BUILD source in the existing ingest framework (follow how lib/directory-steam.ts and lib/directory-ingest plug in): per-source enable flag defaulting OFF except Steam, rate limiting + circuit breaker, normalization into ExternalServer (game family, address, port, name, players, max, map, country if given, source, sourceId, attribution), dedupe, the existing block-other-hosts matcher applied, liveness probing with the right protocol per family. Never store anything the source's terms forbid storing.
4. Customer portal page: find the customer-facing public server directory page(s) (grep app/ for directory; both /game-servers/directory and the dashboard version), ensure external servers are shown with a visible source attribution, a 'live' status, filters by game, and that Nxeon's own servers are visually distinct. Keep the existing Nxeon theme. Add tests for the query and filters.
5. Verify adapters against the real public APIs with a SMALL sample (a few requests per source, polite delays) from the sandbox only, writing results to /root/agent-notes/directory-v2.md, to prove the parsing is right. Do NOT write to the prod DB; use fakes or an in-memory/sqlite style test harness.
6. tsc --noEmit must be 0 errors; tests green.

FINAL REPORT: root cause of 'never ran', the sources table (BUILD vs BLOCKED with reasons), branch/commits/files, how each adapter was verified live, what you could not verify, the exact owner steps to go live (keys, flags, order, legal checks), and the flags it will flip.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, and standard web media types only; one publish sends at most 255 files and 64MB, while a version may hold up to 511 files and 256MB in all, so a larger set goes up over several publishes to the same `url` (each later publish adds to the files already there).

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. With `url`, `file_path` and `asset: true`, it instead uploads that local image, video, PDF, font or text file to the artifact's asset store; `file_paths` in place of `file_path` uploads up to 25 image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in one call under one approval (a text file goes in a call of its own), and the result gives each one's `url`. The page must declare the `assets` capability, and the `artifact-capabilities` skill has the limits. Claude references the uploaded file from the page by the `url` in the result, exactly as given. To reuse assets another artifact already holds, such as a design system's fonts or images, Claude passes `from_url` (that artifact) and up to ten `asset_ids` from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it in place of `file_path`: the server copies them without downloading or re-uploading, and the result gives each copy's new url in this artifact, to reference exactly as given; both artifacts must be ones the person can open. Another artifact's published files are reused through `files` instead: Claude maps a path to {"artifact": "<its url>", "path": "<its published path>"} and that file is copied into the new version server side with its type. Script, style, data, font and image files copy this way; an HTML, SVG or XML document does not, so Claude reads it with `path` and publishes it as its own file.
- **read**: takes `url` (any claude.ai artifact link: claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) and returns the published page's content. Claude reads these links with this action, not with WebFetch or curl, and also uses it wherever a skill or notice says to re-read an artifact. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. **Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

1	# Growth batch brief — Nxeon, 2026-10-02 (applies to every agent in this batch)
2	
3	## Source of truth for your items
4	- Owner decisions: /root/growth/decisions-summary.json (`dec` map; `do` / `change` = approved, `skip` = do NOT build).
5	- Full item write-ups (title, rationale, evidence, effort): /root/growth/*.json and the matching *.md files (marketing-acquisition, product-growth, seo-content, ops). Read the item text for your ids before building; follow its stated approach and honour its caveats.
6	- Prior art and rules: /root/FLEET-STATUS-2026-10-01.md, /root/agent-notes/*.md, repo CLAUDE.md, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.
7	
8	## Hard rules (violating any of these is a failure)
9	1. Never edit, build, test or restart inside /opt/nxeon. Work ONLY in your own git worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-<name> -b <branch> main`. main already contains the day's fixes; branch from current main.
10	2. In the worktree, node_modules and .prisma/@prisma must be REAL copies, never symlinks (see /root/agent-notes/provfix.md). Never run `prisma generate` against /opt/nxeon's client. Use a throwaway Postgres for anything DB-related.
11	3. Take the box-wide heavy lock for builds and test runs: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/heavy.sh (the box is shared by ~7 agents; do not run more than one heavy command at a time).
12	4. Commit with explicit paths only (`git add <paths>`), never `git add -A`. Do not push. Notes go to /root/agent-notes/<name>.md.
13	5. You must not touch production, any Proxmox node, any VM, any customer data, any email/SMS/Discord/social send, any payment or card action, or any paid third-party tool. Everything that sends, charges or posts must be built behind a default-OFF flag or produced as a draft for the owner. Do not deploy; the owner's session merges and promotes.
14	6. Schema changes must be purely additive (the production deploy only runs additive `prisma db push`).
15	7. Honesty: never fabricate statistics, reviews, customer counts, awards or testimonials. Claims must come from real data in the repo/DB or be omitted. The "47 seconds" tagline is intentional brand copy; never flag or change it. Never mention a third-party infrastructure provider to customers; Nxeon speaks as the owner. Customer-visible copy: no "provider".
16	8. Brand: use existing design tokens/components (navy + violet + cyan; brand gradient blue→violet→magenta). Match surrounding code style, naming and comment density. Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md for operational/third-party knowledge.
17	9. Money path (checkout, pricing, billing, Stripe, wallet): extra care. Build behind flags, add tests, and state exactly what was and was not verified. Never run a live charge.
18	10. Legal flags: Hytale and FiveM are legally sensitive (owner decision: no managed FiveM sale without permission). Content for these is informational only, and you must say so in your notes.
19	11. No overlap: stay inside your assigned item ids. If you need a file another agent owns, make the smallest possible change and say so in your notes.
20	12. Verify before reporting: run typecheck and the tests related to your change, and run what you can locally (a local dev render is fine if it uses a throwaway DB; never the shared prod DB). Your final report must list: branch, commits, files touched, what you verified, what you could not verify, any owner decisions or owner actions needed, and any flags/env vars to enable.
21	----
22	# Nxeon Server Directory v2 - research and build plan
23	
24	Date: 2026-10-03. Author: research agent (read-only; nothing in /opt/nxeon, no DB, no keys, no scrapers touched).
25	Status of evidence: I read the repo docs/code and public docs. Where a terms page was blocked (HTTP 403/404 to our fetcher) or I only have secondary sources, the row says UNVERIFIED. This is an engineering risk assessment, not legal advice; the "owner must read" links are the real checkpoints.
26	
27	---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	
29	## 0. Summary table
30	
31	| # | Topic | Recommendation (one line) |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| 1 | Strategy | Build the directory from THREE legitimate inputs, in this order of trust: (a) Nxeon-hosted + customer opt-in, (b) **owner-submitted servers verified by a code in the server's own name/MOTD** (new; works for EVERY game incl. those with no public list), (c) official master-server data (Steam) and a few official game-run lists. Everything is then re-verified by our own direct protocol probe (A2S, Minecraft SLP, Bedrock RakNet ping) so numbers are ours, not copied. |
34	| 2 | Biggest source | Steam master list (~30 of our 48 families). Terms are READABLE and workable but strict: attribute Valve with links (not nofollow), never imply Valve endorsement, disclose storage country in privacy policy, <=100k calls/day, Valve can revoke anytime. Rating AMBER. Owner must read before first apply. |
35	| 3 | Minecraft (Java+Bedrock) | No official list exists. Legit = owner-submitted + MOTD-verified + Nxeon free/paid. Direct SLP/RakNet pings are ours to do. Third-party list sites: do NOT ingest (HTML scraping = RED; their APIs are mostly vote/owner APIs with ToS UNVERIFIED). |
36	| 4 | Aggregators (BattleMetrics, GameMonitoring, serverlist.gg, etc.) | Do NOT bulk-ingest. BattleMetrics API is public (60 req/min anon, 300/min with a token) but its ToS page blocked our fetcher => UNVERIFIED, and republishing their whole product is the likeliest to draw a complaint. At most: on-demand "View on BattleMetrics" link-outs. RED-until-read. |
37	| 5 | Games with NO acceptable public source | Satisfactory, Terraria, Palworld, Core Keeper, Enshrouded (unverified Steam), Dragonwilds, Nightingale, Icarus, Sunkenland?, ARK:SA, Arma Reforger, DST, Factorio (credentialed) -> Nxeon-hosted + opt-in/owner-submitted only. See matrix. |
38	| 6 | Data model | Evolve `ExternalServer` into a provider-agnostic `DirectoryServer` (additive migration): provenance + attribution fields, `verifiedBy`, probe state (`lastProbeAt`, `lastAliveAt`, `consecutiveFails`, `status`), country/region/ASN-free geoip, normalized `tags`/`mode`/`modded`/`passworded`, `claimedBy`, plus new tables `DirectorySource`, `DirectoryOptOut`, `DirectoryReport`, `DirectoryProbeSample`. |
39	| 7 | Ingest | `DirectoryProvider` interface mirroring `lib/modsync` (`Provider`, `requiresEnv`, cursor, token bucket, circuit breaker, kill switches default OFF) + separate **prober** loop in the worker. ~100-150k rows steady state, ~0.6M UDP probes/day, <1 GB/yr storage. Negligible cost if probes come from a node-2 worker, not the primary. |
40	| 8 | UX | Marketing: hub -> game -> (country, mode, "best of") pages, individual server pages ONLY for Nxeon-hosted/claimed servers; strict noindex thresholds. Portal: `/dashboard/servers/browse` with filters, favourites, "Host your own like this" CTA, opt-in listing wizard. |
41	| 9 | Phasing | P1 (3-4 agent-days): turn on existing Valve ingest with attribution + schedule + liveness prober + opt-out. P2 (4-5): owner-submitted + MOTD verification + Minecraft Java/Bedrock. P3 (5-6): provider framework, admin observability, v2 data model UI, portal browse. P4 (4-6): marketing IA (country/mode/best-of pages), claim flow. P5 (optional, owner-gated): Vintage Story, FiveM, Factorio, aggregator link-outs. |
42	| 10 | Owner decisions | 8 listed in section 9. Hard gates: read Steam API terms + add Valve attribution + privacy-policy storage-country line BEFORE `directory_ingest_enabled`; no source goes live without its "legal checkpoint" box ticked. |
43	
44	---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	
46	## 1. What exists today (from code, so the plan builds on it)
47	
48	- `lib/server-directory.ts` (pure core): `DirEntry`, sources `nxeon-paid | nxeon-free | nxeon-community | external`, dedupe by domain/ip/ip:port with `DEFAULT_PORT`, survivor rules (Nxeon > image > described > newest), ordering (image, Nxeon, busiest), `INDEX_MIN_DESCRIBED = 3` within 7 days, `rel="ugc nofollow noopener"` on owner links.
49	- `lib/directory-ingest/valve.ts`: `VALVE_APPIDS` for 11 families (valheim 892970, projectzomboid 108600, rust 252490, cs2 730, tf2 440, gmod 4000, l4d2 550, ark 346110, unturned 304930, sdtd 251570, conan 440900). Calls `https://api.steampowered.com/IGameServersService/GetServerList/v1/?key=..&limit=..&filter=\appid\N\dedicated\1`. Parser drops private IPs, `dedicated:false`, junk names. Never echoes the key in errors. Good.
50	- `lib/directory-ingest/run.ts`: gated by `Setting directory_ingest_enabled`; upsert on `(source, sourceKey)`; drops rows colliding with Nxeon-hosted keys; prunes rows unseen for 3 days. NO liveness probe, NO schedule, NO attribution, NO country, only runs from `scripts/directory-ingest.ts`.
51	- `ExternalServer`: id, source, sourceKey, game, name, host, ip, port, queryPort, map, description, imageUrl, country, players, maxPlayers, version, tags[], connKey, ipKey, hidden, firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt. `DirectoryIngestRun` audit rows. `PublicListingMeta` (tagline, image, website, mediaApproved, hidden, featured). Display gate `directory_external_show` default off.
52	- `lib/modsync/` is the template to copy: `Provider` interface, `registry.ts`, `runner.ts` (one bounded slice per 5-min tick, DB claim, cursor), `http.ts` (UA `NxeonModSync/1.0 (+https://nxeon.cloud; mods@nxeon.cloud)`, token bucket, backoff+jitter, `Retry-After`, ETag), `requiresEnv` -> `needs_key` park for 6 h, admin Run/Pause/Enable/Reset cursor, per-provider verdict doc `docs/MODS-SOURCES.md` ("metadata + link-through unless the licence grants more"). The directory should get the same shape AND the same discipline: a `docs/DIRECTORY-SOURCES.md` verdict table.
53	- Reusable: `lib/geo-ip.ts` (geoip-lite IP->country, local, no network), `lib/game-config.ts` `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` (48 distinct family keys; `projectzomboid` is listed twice in the schema file, which is why the brief says 49), `lib/games.ts` `DEFAULT_PORT` + protocol per family, free-MC `FreePublicServer` (already stores `queryPort`, runs A2S sampling in `FreePublicServerSample` -> a liveness pattern already exists).
54	- Growth items: seo-025 ("only active, described servers indexable; noindex empty/new; rel=ugc; moderation"), seo-026 (Valve list as traffic/backlink magnet; "API ToS UNVERIFIED; ongoing infra cost"), mkt-031 (opt-in + moderation, done).
55	
56	Honest note on seo-026's premise: Steam GetServerList is a *list of addresses and live stats*. The traffic win comes from pages with unique value (country/mode/"best" curation, uptime history, player trend), not from the raw list. Plan accordingly.
57	
58	---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	
60	## 2. SOURCE MATRIX
61	
62	### 2.1 Risk classes (read this first)
63	
64	| Class | What it is | Examples | Default stance |
65	|---|---|---|---|
66	| A. Direct protocol query | We send the game's own query packet (A2S_INFO, MC Status/SLP, RakNet unconnected ping) to an ADDRESS. The protocol is the game's public interface. No third party's database is copied. | A2S UDP, SLP TCP, Bedrock UDP 19132, Quake/Source-engine queries | GREEN, provided the address came from a permitted source and we are polite (rate, no scanning). |
67	| B. Official API / master server operated by the game's publisher | Valve Web API, Vintage Story master, FiveM/Cfx backend, TruckersMP API | GetServerList | AMBER: read terms; attribute; keep keys private; revocable. |
68	| C. Third-party aggregator API | BattleMetrics API, GameMonitoring, etc. | | RED until terms read; their business IS this list. Prefer link-out. |
69	| D. HTML scraping of third-party listing sites | Parsing minecraft-server-list pages, serverlist.gg, top-games.net, etc. | | RED. Almost all such sites forbid automated access in their ToS and/or robots.txt; also database-right/copyright exposure (EU sui generis, contract). NOT RECOMMENDED for any game. Never "just a few pages" at scale. |
70	| E. Active discovery (scanning address space) | Masscan/Shodan-style probing to find servers | | RED (abuse reports, ISP AUP, legal). Never. We only probe addresses we were given or learned from A/B sources. |
71	| F. Owner-submitted | A server owner submits their own address and proves control. | | GREEN (consent + verification). Our main answer for games without a list. |
72	
73	Key principle: ADDRESSES and live status are the minimum data we need. Names/descriptions from strangers are untrusted text (already sanitised by `cleanText`).
74	
75	### 2.2 Per-source detail
76	
77	Rating key: GREEN low, AMBER read-before-launch, RED do not use. "Terms" column states what I actually read vs. UNVERIFIED.
78	
79	**S1. Steam master list: `IGameServersService/GetServerList` (and the UDP master protocol)**
80	- Access: HTTPS with a free Steam Web API key (we do not yet hold one; the owner must register; I did not). `filter=\appid\N\dedicated\1`, `limit` (code caps at 5000). Alternative with NO key: the UDP Master Server Query Protocol at `hl2master.steampowered.com:27011` (https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Master_Server_Query_Protocol). It is throttled by Valve and paginated by IP; the Web API is easier and more reliable. The Web API terms below only cover the Web API; the UDP protocol is documented on the Valve Developer Community wiki but I found no usage terms either way (UNVERIFIED) - so do not treat it as a way around the terms.
81	- Data: addr (ip:queryPort), gameport, name, appid, gamedir, version, region (Steam region id), players, max_players, bots, map, secure (VAC), dedicated, os, gametype (tag string). Not given: country (we geoip), description, uptime, ping (we measure), website.
82	- Cadence: list is live; sweep every 30-60 min is plenty (stats age fast). Rate limit: terms say 100,000 calls/day (our need: <=11-35 games x 24-48 sweeps = <2k/day). 
83	- Terms: READ https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apiterms on 2026-10-03. Clauses that matter:
84	  - "You may not present the Steam Data ... so that it appears (a) that your Application is endorsed or affiliated with Valve or Steam, or (b) to be available from a third party."
85	  - Must "implement the Valve name(s), logo(s), and links to Valve ... on any Web page incorporating the Steam Web API and/or Steam Data" per the Steam Web API documentation, and may not "tag links to Valve ... with a 'nofollow' attribute" (so the attribution link must be a plain followed link; our existing rel="ugc nofollow" rule must NOT be applied to it).
86	  - "You will inform the end user about any Steam Data you will store, and you will store the Steam Data in a country (or countries) identified in your privacy policy."
87	  - "limited to one hundred thousand (100,000) calls to the Steam Web API per day."
88	  - Valve "may change, suspend or discontinue the Steam Web API and suspend or terminate your use ... at any time for any reason, without notice."
89	  - Key must stay confidential, not shared with third parties (we only call server-side).
90	  - Also "You will only retrieve Steam Data about a Steam end user as requested by the end user" - applies to user profile data; server lists are not user data, but we must NEVER add any Steam-ID/player-name fetch to the directory. (A2S_PLAYER names are player data: do NOT store.)
91	- Caching/republishing: terms contain no explicit caching-duration limit and no explicit ban on public display of server-list data, but they are written around an "Application" and end users, so using it for a public SEO directory is an interpretation, not an explicit grant. Honest rating: **AMBER**. Mitigation = literal compliance with the three clauses above, plus our own A2S re-verification (the numbers we show are ours, taken from the server directly, with Steam only as the way we learned the address).
92	- Attribution text (proposal): footer on every page that shows Steam-discovered servers: "Server addresses discovered via the Steam master server list. Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks of Valve Corporation. Nxeon is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve." with a followed link to https://store.steampowered.com/ and the Valve name/logo as the docs require (owner/designer must check the exact current brand-asset rules in the Steamworks Web API docs: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi - behind a login wall for some pages, UNVERIFIED). NOTE a tension: clause (b) "available from a third party" - our UI must not say "list provided by X"; saying "discovered via Steam" is attribution, not offering it as someone else's.
93	- Steam trademark/IP: we also must not use Steam store art as covers without checking its licence. Current covers are the owner's own art; keep it that way.
94	- Families it covers (appid MUST be verified per game before enabling; ids beyond the 11 already in code are from memory and UNVERIFIED): valheim, rust, cs2, tf2, gmod, l4d2, cs16 (appid 10), projectzomboid, ark (ASE), unturned, sdtd, conan, dayz (221100), arma3 (107410), squad (393380), mordhau (629760), kf2 (232090), sandstorm (581320), barotrauma (602960), spaceengineers (244850), empyrion (383120), stationeers (544550), theforest (242760), sonsoftheforest (1326470), vrising (1604030, servers have a ListOnSteam option), abioticfactor (427410), soulmask (2646460), necesse (1169040), theisle (376210), enshrouded (1203620, UNVERIFIED that servers are on the master list). Procedure: owner-approved one-off test call per appid; if the sample returns 0 rows, the game goes to the "no public source" bucket.
95	- Gotchas: (1) returned `addr` port is the QUERY port; join port is `gameport` (existing parser handles). Some games (Rust) fine, Source-engine games where `gameport`=0 -> query port. (2) Very large lists (Rust, CS2, CS 1.6, GMod: likely 5-30k rows each; UNVERIFIED sizes) -> `limit` cap hides the tail; rank by players or filter `\empty\0`/`\noplayers`. (3) Honeypot/spam servers: ~10-20% of public Source lists are fake/"player count spoofed" (well known problem): our own A2S probe + a sanity rule (players <= max, reject max>128 for most games, reject names that are only URLs) removes most.
96	
97	**S2. Minecraft Java: Server List Ping (direct)**
98	- Access: TCP handshake+status request on host:port (default 25565), JSON status with version, players online/max, sample, description (MOTD), favicon (base64 PNG 64x64). Protocol doc: https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Server_List_Ping (was wiki.vg). No key, no login, no terms - the protocol is how every client lists servers. Rating: GREEN as a protocol, but ONLY for addresses given/permitted. We need a source of addresses (below).
99	- Do NOT store the player `sample` names (personal data, and unnecessary). Do NOT use the favicon as a cover unless the owner approved it (user content; it could be offensive): treat like customer images (review first).
100	- Cadence: per-server probe every 10-15 min for listed servers (cheap: ~1 KB). Rate: one connection per server per probe; hard cap per destination IP (hosting providers run hundreds of servers per IP; cap 1 probe/s per IP).
101	- Mojang rules that affect the site (not the data): Minecraft EULA https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/eula and Usage Guidelines https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/usage-guidelines. Per secondary sources: don't use Mojang/Minecraft brand elements in a way that implies affiliation, "Minecraft" not as the first word of a name, and include a "not affiliated with Mojang AB or Microsoft" disclaimer (primary page not re-read by me: UNVERIFIED wording; the disclaimer is cheap and the existing /servers pages likely already carry something - check).
102	- Address sources (decide per row below): (a) Nxeon free + paid MC (already), (b) owner-submitted + MOTD verification, (c) third-party lists = see S9.
103	
104	**S3. Minecraft Bedrock: RakNet Unconnected Ping (direct)**
105	- Access: UDP 19132 (IPv6 19133), "unconnected ping" -> pong with MOTD string `MCPE;name;protocol;version;players;max;serverId;worldName;gamemode;...`. Fields (from memory, UNVERIFIED until a sample is read): name, ip:port, players, max, gamemode, version, mods, whitelisted, password flag.
110	- Terms: I found no published API terms (UNVERIFIED). It is the publisher's own client endpoint; low abuse risk if we poll politely (1 request / 30 min, with UA) and attribute. content.content:
# dirp1 (2026-10-04) branch feature/directory-phase1 (on top of feature/directory-block-other-hosts), worktree /tank/nxeon-wt-dirp1, commit b872644638
Directory phase 1: Steam ingest production-ready. See docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Steam ingest and liveness" (go-live runbook inside).
- Pure: lib/directory-ingest/{a2s,schedule}.ts, lib/directory-liveness.ts, lib/directory-steam.ts. DB: gates.ts, sweep.ts, prober.ts. Worker: worker/directory.ts (2 sweeps in worker/index.ts).
- Additive schema: ExternalServer probe cols, DirectoryIngestRun blocked/status/trigger/note, DirectorySource table. Needs prisma db push BEFORE code.
- Edited shared: lib/settings.ts (7 keys), lib/actions-listing.ts, lib/server-directory(-data).ts, marketing template tools/nxm/native/server-directory (regen via port_pages.py), worker/index.ts (+2 lines).
- Tests: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://x:x@localhost:5432/x npx tsx --test test/directory-{a2s,liveness,sweep}.test.ts; DB test needs DIRECTORY_TEST_DATABASE_URL (throwaway PG; mine was /tank/pg-dirp1 port 54399, removed).
- Full suite has 46 PRE-EXISTING failures (identical on the blocklist branch without my changes).
- Hazard learned: `git stash` is shared across worktrees; do not use it in a worktree.
- Never run: Steam API, A2S to real hosts. All fixtures synthetic.
| vintagestory | Official master list (S4) | HTTP | name, players, mods, version | P5 (permission email first). |
| fivem | Cfx.re frontend (S6, undocumented) | single/<code> | name, players, tags | NX + OS in v2; crawl RED/AMBER. |
| eco | Strange Loop publishes a server list in-game; public endpoint UNVERIFIED (https://play.eco/) | ? | - | Research item; default NX + OS. |
| ets2 / ats | TruckersMP official only (S7) | - | - | NX only; skip. |

Games for which I recommend NO public ingest at all (leave to NX + opt-in + owner-submitted): satisfactory, terraria, palworld, factorio (until credentialed decision), corekeeper, dragonwilds, nightingale, icarus, sunkenland, dst, fivem, arkasa, armareforger, ets2, ats, eco (until verified), enshrouded (until Steam sample).

Realistic coverage: ~25-30 of 48 families can have a Steam-sourced public list; ~15 stay "Nxeon + owner-submitted". Say so on the hub honestly ("Servers hosted on Nxeon and servers whose owners listed them").

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. DATA MODEL

### 3.1 Principle
Keep the pure `DirEntry` core and dedupe unchanged (connKey/ipKey). Rename conceptually: `ExternalServer` -> directory rows from any provider. Do additive Prisma changes (the repo has no `migrations/` dir, schema is pushed: be careful, all additive/nullable, per MEMORY note on schema rollback).

### 3.2 `ExternalServer` additions (nullable or defaulted)
```
provider        String   // replaces meaning of `source`: "steam" | "owner" | "vintagestory" | "fivem" | ...  (keep `source` for back-compat; backfill provider = source)
attributionKey  String?  // "steam" -> which footer/attribution block to render
verifiedBy      String?  // null | "provider" | "probe" | "token" | "nxeon"
verifiedAt      DateTime?
claimedByUserId String?  // owner who claimed/submitted (FK User, SetNull)
claimToken      String?  // hashed; never exposed
// liveness (written by the prober, not by the ingest)
status          String   @default("UNKNOWN") // UNKNOWN | ALIVE | DEGRADED | DEAD
lastProbeAt     DateTime?
lastAliveAt     DateTime?
consecutiveFails Int     @default(0)
latencyMs       Int?     // our measured RTT from the probe node (label "ping from <region>")
probeKind       String?  // "a2s" | "slp" | "raknet" | "tcp" | "http"
uptime7d        Float?   // from DirectoryProbeSample rollups
// geo
country         String?  // ISO-2 via lib/geo-ip.ts at insert/IP change
region          String?  // continent code (EU/NA/SA/AS/OC/AF) derived from country
// taxonomy (normalised; raw source tags kept in `tags`)
mode            String?  // game-specific enum, e.g. minecraft: survival|skyblock|factions|...; rust: vanilla|modded|...
modded          Boolean?
passworded      Boolean?
os              String?
categories      String[] // our taxonomy slugs (section 3.5)
flags           Json?    // per-game extras: {"vac":true,"wipe":"weekly","crossplay":true}
// moderation
hidden          Boolean  @default(false) // exists
hiddenReason    String?  // "optout" | "spam" | "report" | "admin"
reportCount     Int      @default(0)
ownerNote       String?  // the owner's description (moderated, rel=ugc)
@@index([game, status, hidden, players])
@@index([country, game])
@@index([provider, lastSeenAt])
```
Keep `connKey/ipKey` + `@@unique([source, sourceKey])`. Uniqueness across providers stays enforced at read time by the pure dedupe; add a **write-time** guard: before insert, if another row has the same `connKey`, merge (provider list array `providers String[]`) instead of creating a second row, so counts per source remain honest.

### 3.3 New tables
- `DirectorySource` (one row per provider): `key`, `enabled` (default false), `showPublic` (default false), `scheduleMinutes`, `lastRunAt`, `lastOkAt`, `lastError`, `consecutiveErrors`, `circuitOpenUntil`, `cursor`, `needsKey`, `termsReviewedBy`, `termsReviewedAt`, `termsUrl`, `attributionText`. The "terms reviewed" fields are a hard gate: provider cannot be enabled unless set (legal checkpoint made mechanical).
- `DirectoryProbeSample` (keep small): `serverId`, `at`, `alive`, `players`, `rttMs`; retain 14 days at 15-30-min grain for ALIVE rows only; roll up to `uptime7d` and a daily peak table `DirectoryDaily(serverId, day, peak, avg, uptimePct)` for 90 days. Only for servers shown or candidates for pages (not all 150k: sample the top ~10k).
- `DirectoryOptOut`: `kind` (ip | ip:port | hostname | cidr | connKey-hash), `value`, `reason`, `requestedBy` (email hash), `verifiedAt`, `createdAt`. Consulted by EVERY provider's upsert and by the prober (never probe an opted-out address).
- `DirectoryReport`: `serverId`, `reason` (spam|abuse|not-mine|offensive|wrong-info), `reporterIpHash`, `note`, `status`. Auto-hide at N distinct reporters pending review.
- `DirectorySubmission`: owner-submitted pending verification (`game`, `address`, `token`, `expiresAt`, `userId`, `attempts`).

### 3.4 Liveness and pruning
- Prober is separate from ingest: it takes rows by `lastProbeAt ASC` within tiers: shown/high-traffic every 15 min; the rest every 6 h; DEAD rows every 24 h then stop.
- State machine: ALIVE -> 2 consecutive failed probes = DEGRADED (shown with a "may be offline" tag? No: hide from pages, keep in admin) -> 6 failures / 24 h = DEAD (hidden everywhere) -> deleted after 7 days dead (3 days for Steam rows, as today) or if the source stops listing it. Rows from owner-submitted: stay 30 days dead before removal + email the owner.
- A row needs BOTH: source says present within TTL AND last probe alive within 24 h, to appear publicly. Steam-only rows with an unprobeable game get TTL 24 h and a "listed on Steam" label, never "online".
- Players/max shown with "updated N min ago" (already the rule). Never show a number older than 60 min as "live".
- Reject lies: `players > max`, `max > game cap`, probe name differs wildly from source name (hijacked listing), identical (name,players) across >20 IPs (spam farm).

### 3.5 Taxonomy (categories/tags)
- Per-game mode enums live in a new `lib/directory-taxonomy.ts` keyed by family, derived from `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` where possible (e.g. rust: vanilla/modded/softcore, wipe cycle, pvp/pve; minecraft: survival, skyblock, factions, minigames, creative, prison, towny, roleplay, modded, bedrock-crossplay, anarchy; gmod: darkrp, ttt, sandbox, prophunt, murder; valheim: pve, pvp, hardcore, modded, vanilla+; pz: vanilla, build-42, roleplay, hardcore).
- Mapping order: owner-set > source tags (`gametype`, MOTD keywords) via per-game keyword rules > unset. Always store the evidence; unknown stays null, never guess ("nothing is invented" rule from valve.ts).
- Global facets: country, region, passworded, modded, players band, language (only if owner-set), uptime band, "Hosted on Nxeon".

### 3.6 Abuse/spam, safety, privacy
- Display ONLY: name (sanitised), a public join address (ip:port or domain:port, already what the source publishes), game, mode, map, players/max, version, country. Never: A2S_PLAYER names, Steam IDs, admin contacts, RCON/query ports unless the join port equals them, hosting node IPs of Nxeon servers (existing rule), SLP player samples, owner email, internal IDs.
- Address hygiene: reject private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/multicast/our own ranges (extend the existing regex to include 100.64/10, 224/4, 240/4, IPv6 equivalents); resolve hostnames once, pin the resolved IP for the probe, reject if it resolves to private (SSRF) and re-check on each probe (DNS rebinding). Ports < 1024 and well-known service ports (22, 25, 53, 80, 443, 3306...) rejected (a "game server" at :22 is a port scan vector).
- Probe politeness: global pps cap, per-destination-IP cap (1/s, max 4 concurrent), per-/24 cap, jittered schedule, UA/identification in the TCP-level payload where the protocol allows, a public page `/directory/probe-info` explaining who we are and how to opt out (put abuse@ contact), honour opt-out within 24 h, run from a node-2 worker (blast radius away from the primary's IP reputation, which also sends email).
- Name moderation: strip control/RTL chars (existing), collapse markup/colour codes (Minecraft section sign, FiveM ^1, Unity rich text), run a word filter (slurs/porn/gambling) -> auto-hide + admin queue; never render HTML; images only after review.
- Spam controls for owner-submitted: Nxeon account + verified email required, 5 pending/ 20 total listings per account, probe token verification, cool-down, captcha on anonymous (if we allow anonymous - recommend NO).
- GDPR/privacy: a server IP of a home-hosted server can be personal data; basis = legitimate interest + easy opt-out; update privacy policy (also REQUIRED by the Steam terms: country of storage + what Steam data is stored); retention as above; no player-level data at all.
- Takedown/opt-out: public `/directory/remove` form: enter address -> we probe and show a token to put in the server name OR the owner emails from the domain's WHOIS/abuse contact OR logs in as the Nxeon owner. Verified requests insert `DirectoryOptOut` immediately (row hidden at once; permanent exclusion). Unverified urgent requests (abuse/safety/DMCA-like) -> admin can hide on trust with a 7-day verification window. SLA stated on the page: 72 h max, target 24 h.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

# AdvertiseServer Function

Based on the wiki documentation, `AdvertiseServer` controls whether your server appears in the public listing. When set to `true`, the server publishes information to a master server.

The setting enables your server to be listed publicly. According to the documentation: "Whether or not add this server to the master server (public server listing)."

To use this feature, you must configure `ServerName` (4–80 characters). The wiki notes that `ServerName` is "visible in the public server listing" and "must be set for 'AdvertiseServer' to function."

The default master server URL is: `"http://masterserver.vintagestory.at/api/v1/servers/"`

OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens are used for authorization, and personal access tokens can be created from the developers area.

content.thinking:
I should only keep servers that are truly public—no password and not whitelisted—and skip passworded ones since they aren't actually joinable. For hostname-based rows without a resolvable IP, I'll judge by hostname rather than IP, and I'm noting that tops.vintagestory.at is the official server listing.

For TruckersMP, I'm mapping their listing rows into the same schema: game, ip, port, name, online count, max players, queue, keyed by ip:port, with ETS2/ATS game tags and promods/shortname tags, attributed to truckersmp, with liveness driven directly by their reported online flag rather than an A2S probe.

For listing-type providers generally, I'll set probeStatus directly from the provider's own online flag at ingest time rather than running my own probe, since the master server already handles staleness. That said, I still need real protocol-level liveness probers (slp, raknet, etc.) implemented per family even though no current source feeds those address types yet, per the task requirements.

I'm defining a `probeKindFor(game)` mapping: Minecraft Java goes to slp, Bedrock to raknet, Steam A2S families to a2s, Vintage Story to tcp, ETS2/ATS to listing, and anything else to null so it just relies on listing TTL instead of active probing. Legacy rows with a null probeKind default to a2s for backward compatibility, and I'm reusing the existing server-query ping functions for slp/raknet with proper timeouts, then building out a separate provider-run.ts to keep this generalized ingestion logic apart from the existing Valve-specific ingest path.

Now I'm sketching a generic `DirectoryProvider` interface with a `ProviderCandidate` shape covering host, ip, ports, player counts, and probe metadata, plus fetch and probeKind methods per provider. For rate limiting I'm planning an HTTP helper with minimum request intervals, a proper user agent, timeouts, and response size caps, and I'm trying to figure out where to stash ETag values since DirectorySource doesn't have a dedicated cursor field -- possibly repurposing the stats JSON column, though that risks being overwritten elsewhere.
